rows.title: Ivanka and Jared took a massive income hit in their final year at the White House
rows.standfirst: Senior White House aides Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump reported $120 million in income for 2020, a share drop from prior years.

rows.title: A U.S. housing crisis could be looming on the horizon
rows.standfirst: At the end of March, more than 600,000 Americans will once again be on the hook to make monthly mortgage payments.

rows.title: Your home’s value may have soared nearly 10% during the pandemic
rows.standfirst: If you’d asked most sharp observers to predict what would happen to housing if joblessness exploded and the economy cratered, few would have foreseen a boom in which prices jumped but at the same time houses got cheaper to carry.

rows.title: When could $1,400 stimulus checks go out? Here’s what we know so far
rows.standfirst: At this rate, a third round of stimulus checks could be deposited before the first day of spring.

rows.title: Biden extends foreclosure moratorium, mortgage relief measures through June
rows.standfirst: President Biden has taken further steps to alleviate the coronavirus pandemic’s economic impact on American homeowners.

rows.title: ‘Not the time to be concerned about a big crash’ say stock market strategists
rows.standfirst: “The time to panic is going to be if the Fed starts tightening financial conditions, and as long as the Fed has no intention of doing that, it gives you more room to run,” says one strategist.

rows.title: Bitcoin is proving it’s not the hedge against inflation that some boosters claim
rows.standfirst: “Bitcoin dropped by 20%, but inflation expectations didn’t drop by 20%,” observes one analyst. “They didn’t drop at all.”

rows.title: Rent prices show biggest one-month growth since the start of the pandemic
rows.standfirst: The days of lower rates seem to be coming to an end.

rows.title: Investor jitters go global
rows.standfirst: U.S. futures are off their lows as global stocks grow more volatile.

rows.title: Buying a new home? Expect to pay $24,000 more as the worsening lumber shortage pushes wood prices up 180%
rows.standfirst: The pandemic has caused lumber demand to spike and supply to fall. The perfect storm has prices up 180%.
